title: GE4u Dental English Starter Pack
subtitle: Core vocabulary for dental students
disclaimer: Educational English-learning material only. It is not a clinical protocol or a substitute for faculty-approved textbooks and clinical supervision.

words.definition: A hard structure in the mouth used for biting and chewing.
words.example: The tooth is sensitive to cold drinks.

words.definition: The hard outer covering of the crown of a tooth.
words.example: Enamel protects the underlying tissues of the tooth.

words.definition: The hard tissue beneath enamel and cementum.
words.example: Dentin may become sensitive when it is exposed.

words.definition: The soft tissue inside a tooth containing nerves and blood vessels.
words.example: The dental pulp contains nerves and blood vessels.

words.definition: The soft tissue that surrounds the teeth and covers the jawbone.
words.example: Healthy gingiva is usually firm and does not bleed easily.

words.definition: A sticky biofilm that forms on tooth surfaces.
words.example: Dental plaque can contribute to gingival inflammation.

words.definition: A disease process that causes demineralisation and damage to tooth structure.
words.example: The dentist detected dental caries during the examination.

words.definition: Inflammation of the gingiva, commonly associated with dental plaque.
words.example: Bleeding during brushing can be a sign of gingivitis.

words.definition: An inflammatory disease affecting the supporting tissues of the teeth.
words.example: Periodontitis can lead to loss of periodontal attachment.

words.definition: An abnormal relationship between the upper and lower teeth when the jaws close.
words.example: The orthodontist assessed the patient's malocclusion.

words.definition: An unpleasant odour of the breath.
words.example: The patient asked about persistent halitosis.

words.definition: Pain in or around a tooth.
words.example: The patient reported a severe toothache at night.

words.definition: An assessment of the oral cavity, teeth, gingiva and related structures.
words.example: An oral examination is part of the initial dental assessment.

words.definition: An image produced using X-rays for diagnostic assessment.
words.example: The dentist reviewed the dental radiograph.

words.definition: A filling or other material used to restore damaged tooth structure.
words.example: The restoration was checked for marginal integrity.

words.definition: The removal of a tooth from its socket.
words.example: The dentist explained the extraction procedure.

words.definition: A negative reproduction of oral structures used to make a model or appliance.
words.example: The clinician took an impression of the upper arch.

words.definition: A medicine that temporarily blocks sensation in a limited area.
words.example: The dentist discussed the use of a local anaesthetic.

words.definition: The main problem or symptom that brings a patient to seek care.
words.example: What is your chief complaint today?

words.definition: Information about a person's past and current health conditions and treatments.
words.example: Please tell me about your medical history.

words.definition: An immune-mediated reaction to a substance that is usually harmless to most people.
words.example: Do you have any known drug allergies?

words.meaning: đồng thuận sau khi được cung cấp thông tin
words.definition: Voluntary agreement after receiving and understanding relevant information about a procedure.
words.example: The clinician obtained informed consent before the procedure.

words.definition: A planned visit after an initial consultation or treatment.
words.example: Please book a follow-up appointment in two weeks.

words.definition: Guidance provided to a patient for care and recovery after an operation.
words.example: The patient received written postoperative instructions.

words.definition: An instrument used to view oral surfaces indirectly and retract soft tissues.
words.example: The dentist used a dental mirror to inspect the lingual surface.

words.meaning: thám trâm nha chu / đầu dò
words.definition: A slender instrument used to examine a surface or measure a periodontal pocket.
words.example: The clinician used a periodontal probe during the assessment.

words.definition: An instrument used to remove deposits from tooth surfaces.
words.example: The hygienist selected a scaler for deposit removal.

words.definition: A tooth-coloured restorative material made from a resin matrix and filler particles.
words.example: Composite resin was selected for the restoration.

words.definition: A device that holds impression material while an impression is made.
words.example: The assistant prepared an impression tray.

words.definition: A validated process intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life.
words.example: Reusable instruments must undergo the required cleaning and sterilisation process.

quiz.q: Which structure is the hard outer covering of the crown of a tooth?
quiz.explanation: Enamel covers the crown and protects the underlying tooth tissues.

quiz.q: Which term means inflammation of the gingiva?
quiz.explanation: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gingiva.
A radiograph is an image produced using X-rays.

quiz.q: Which phrase means the main problem that brings a patient to seek care?
quiz.explanation: The chief complaint is the patient's main reason for seeking care.

quiz.q: Which instrument is used to inspect oral surfaces indirectly?
quiz.explanation: A dental mirror provides indirect vision and can retract soft tissues.

quiz.q: What does 'dental caries' mean in Vietnamese?
quiz.explanation: Dental caries is commonly translated as sâu răng.

quiz.q: Which term describes voluntary agreement after relevant information is explained?
quiz.explanation: Informed consent involves understanding relevant information and agreeing voluntarily.

options: A material used to restore damaged tooth structure
quiz.answer: A material used to restore damaged tooth structure
quiz.explanation: A restoration repairs or replaces damaged tooth structure.

quiz.q: Which term refers to an unpleasant odour of the breath?
Which process is intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life from reusable instruments?
quiz.explanation: Sterilisation is a validated process to eliminate microbial life.
